title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A retired couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that used a fake investment interface. A scammer contacted them through WhatsApp and directed them to a mobile trading app. The underlying app was legitimate, but the scammer displayed a fraudulent overlay or "ghost site" that showed false account balances and investment returns on the victim's screen. This created the false impression that money was being successfully invested and could be withdrawn.

The deception succeeded because it exploited a gap between what the victim saw and what was actually happening in the system. The scammer built trust by allowing small successful transactions before requesting larger investments. Catching this fraud would have required either direct verification of account status through the app provider's official channels, or the kind of institutional friction that legitimate financial services impose through identity verification and direct communication outside the scammer's controlled channel.

It is not established whether the mobile app developers or platform operators were aware the app was being used for fraud, or what security measures they had in place to detect or prevent this type of account hijacking or overlay attack.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that began when a stranger contacted them through WhatsApp. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest money using a mobile trading app, initially allowing him to make small trades and withdraw funds to build trust. Over time, the investments grew larger. When Jerry attempted to make a larger withdrawal, he discovered the fraud. Police determined that while the app was legitimate, scammers had created an artificial ghost site that displayed false investment information on his screen.

The couple, Jerry and Mindy Dunaway, are now warning others about the sophisticated tactics used by these criminals. They have been devastated financially and emotionally by the loss of their life savings. Gwinnett County police are investigating the case, though authorities indicate that victims in similar situations rarely recover their stolen funds. The Dunaways' children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help their parents with daily expenses as they work to rebuild their lives.
